# Conditional and Latent Representations

Also called: Conditional Radiance Fields, Latent Code NeRFs

## Overview
Conditional and Latent Representations extend the standard NeRF architecture [14428-sparse-view-and-few-shot-optimization.md] to model an entire class of objects (e.g., chairs) rather than a single static scene [S1]. By conditioning the radiance field on per-instance latent vectors for shape and appearance, this family enables efficient representation of multiple 3D instances within a shared network backbone, allowing for instance-specific editing and novel view synthesis without training separate models for each object [S1]. It differs from sibling methods like [Conditional Radiance Field Training](15963-conditional-radiance-field-training.md) by focusing on the architectural mechanism of injecting latent codes into the network, whereas specific implementations vary in how they decouple shape and color representations [S1].

## Shared principles
The core mechanism involves a neural network $F$ that maps a 3D location $\mathbf{x}$, viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$, and instance-specific latent codes $\mathbf{z}^{(s)}$ (shape) and $\mathbf{z}^{(c)}$ (color) to radiance $\mathbf{c}$ and density $\sigma$ [S1]:
$$
(\mathbf{c}, \sigma) = F(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d}, \mathbf{z}^{(s)}, \mathbf{z}^{(c)})
$$
The density output $\sigma$ is typically independent of the viewing direction, while the radiance $\mathbf{c}$ depends on both position and viewing direction [S1]. Rendering follows the standard volume rendering integral [S1]:
$$
\hat{C}(r, \mathbf{z}^{(s)}, \mathbf{z}^{(c)}) = \sum_{i=1}^{N_c} T_i \alpha_i \mathbf{c}_i
$$
where $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$, $\delta_i = t_{i+1} - t_i$, and $T_i = \exp(-\sum_{j=1}^{i-1} \sigma_j \delta_j)$ [S1]. The latent codes $\mathbf{z}^{(s)}$ and $\mathbf{z}^{(c)}$ are learned parameters optimized jointly with the network weights during training [S1].

## Subtopics

### [Conditional Radiance Field Training](15963-conditional-radiance-field-training.md)
A method that explicitly decouples shape and color codes, injecting them into the embedding layers of a shared coarse/fine MLP backbone. It differs from siblings by separating the injection points for shape and color codes to facilitate independent editing. Choose this when instance-specific editing of geometry and texture is required with a shared network structure.

### [Conditional Radiance Field with Shared Branch](15964-conditional-radiance-field-with-shared-branch.md)
An architecture designed for shape and color disentanglement by separating the geometric representation into shared and instance-specific branches. It differs from siblings by using distinct MLPs for shared shape, instance-specific shape, and fusion, allowing specific submodules to be fine-tuned independently. Choose this when high-fidelity view synthesis and efficient instance-specific editing are prioritized over parameter sharing.

### Conditional Radiance Field
#### definition
- [S1] A neural network representation that extends NeRF to model an entire object class (e.g., chairs) rather than a single scene, using latent vectors for shape and appearance to allow editing.
- [S1] The network $F$ takes a 3D location $\mathbf{x}$, viewing direction $\mathbf{d}$, and instance-specific latent vectors $\mathbf{z}^{(s)}$ and $\mathbf{z}^{(c)}$ to output radiance $\mathbf{c}$ and density $\sigma$.
- [S1] The density output $\sigma$ is independent of the viewing direction.
- [S1] The radiance output $\mathbf{c}$ depends on both position and viewing direction.

#### step
- [S1] Sample $N_c$ 3D points $\{t_i\}_{i=1}^{N_c}$ along a cast ray $r$ from pixel location, ordered near to far.
- [S1] Compute radiance $\mathbf{c}_i$ and density $\sigma_i$ at each sampled point $t_i$ using network $F$.

#### formula
- [S1] Alpha compositing value: $\alpha_i = 1 - \exp(-\sigma_i \delta_i)$, where $\delta_i = t_{i+1} - t_i$ is the distance between adjacent samples.

#### parameter
- [S1] $\mathbf{x}$: 3D location vector $(x, y, z)$.
- [S1] $\mathbf{d}$: viewing direction vector $(\phi, \theta)$.
- [S1] $\mathbf{z}^{(c)}$: latent color (appearance) vector.

#### layout
- [S1] Network $F$ is parametrized as a multi-layer perceptron (MLP).

## Background
The concept of conditional radiance fields was introduced in "Editing Conditional Radiance Fields" (ICCV 2021) [S1]. It builds upon the original NeRF representation [45] to enable editing over entire shape classes. The method allows for the disentanglement of shape and appearance, facilitating modifications to specific parts of the network during editing tasks [S1].
